Plan to shipment

Take a sales order stock cannot cover through planning, buying and building to a confirmed shipment.

Status
Walked 3 of 7
Module
Sales, Enterprise Planning, Procurement, Manufacturing, Warehousing
Length
7 tasks, 52 steps
Updated
22 Oct 2026
Applies to
Infor LN

Start

Summary

TaskWhat you doResultSteps
1PreflightAll three items are plannable, and every on-hand figure is written down.5
2Create the demandA sales order for more pairs than exist, inside the order horizon.7
3Run MRPPlanned orders cover the shortfall and reconcile in the pegging tree.6
4Cross the boundaryThe proposals become a real purchase order and a real production order.8
5Receive the componentsRods and sleeves are on hand at the raw-material warehouse.8

Before you start

  • Know each item's stock before you start: Check an item's inventory.
  • The bamboo family as section 2 describes it. If any of it is missing, Create test items builds it and Make the item visible to planning adds the planning data.

Procedure

1Preflight

Result
All three items are plannable, and every on-hand figure is written down.
Screen
Warehousing➔Inventory 360 (whwmd4300m000)

Why LN works this way. Nothing yet. This chain fails silently in two places, an item with no planning data and a component whose stock already covers the requirement, and both are decided by figures readable before anything is created. The Item Order Plan shows whether each item is plannable; Inventory 360 shows what MRP will net against.

StepActionYou should see
1.1Open Inventory 360 (whwmd4300m000)The item filter
1.2Type BAM-CHOP-PAIR in the filter box above the grid's Item column, press Enter, tick its row and click Warehouse Inventory. Read its row for the finished-goods warehouseWrite downpair on-hand before andshipping warehouse
1.3Close that tab, untick the row, and do the same for BAM-ROD and then BAM-SLEEVE at the raw-materials warehouseWrite downrod on-hand beforesleeve on-hand before
1.4Open Item Order Plan (cprrp0520m000) and search each of the three items in turnEach one appears. An item that does not is invisible to MRP
1.5For any item that does not appear, add its cluster row. Follow steps 3–5The item now appears — an empty plan, but a plan
Preflight: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
An item is absent from the Item Order PlanIt has no cluster row. Step 1.5. Not an error state; nothing will tell you

2Create the demand

Result
A sales order for more pairs than exist, inside the order horizon.
Screen
Sales➔Orders➔Order Intake Workbench (tdsls4601m200)

Why LN works this way. A sales order for more pairs than exist creates the shortfall the rest of the chain answers. Planning will see it only if its delivery date falls inside the item's order horizon, which LN computes in workdays on a calendar, and the order is approved now because Ship's release needs it, not because planning does.

StepActionYou should see
2.1Create a sales order for BAM-CHOP-PAIR. Follow steps 1–11, with Warehouse from step 1.2An order at Free
2.2Set Ordered Quantity above the on-hand from step 1.2Write downsales order numberordered quantity
2.3Set Planned Delivery Date a few days outWrite downplanned delivery date
2.4Actions➔ApproveStatus = In Process
2.5Open Items - Planning (cprpd1100m000) for BAM-CHOP-PAIR, Horizons tab, and read the Order Horizon dateWrite downorder horizon date
2.6If the date from step 2.2 falls beyond it, raise the Order Horizon days until it does notThe displayed date moves past your delivery date
2.7Reopen Item Order Plan (cprrp0520m000) for BAM-CHOP-PAIRA Sales Order row with your number and quantity as Demand
Create the demand: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
LN refuses the item on the sales orderNo row for the order's sales office on the Sales Offices tab of Item (tcibd0501m100). Add it, then close and reopen the order session
The demand does not appear in the Item Order PlanThe delivery date is beyond the Order Horizon date. Step 2.6 — and the date is not today plus your days

3Run MRP

Result
Planned orders cover the shortfall and reconcile in the pegging tree.

Why LN works this way. MRP nets the demand against stock and generates a planned production order for the pairs, then, through the BOM, planned purchase orders for the rods the pairs need. The arithmetic in the pegging tree is the test that it did so correctly.

StepActionYou should see
3.1Open Generate Order Planning (Item) (cprrp1220m000) for BAM-CHOP-PAIRScenario ACT and Plan Item are set
3.2Select Include Child ItemsThe run will plan the rods and sleeves too
3.3Run the generationThe run completes
3.4Open Item Order Plan (cprrp0520m000) for BAM-CHOP-PAIR and read the planned supply rowWrite downplanned production orderSupply equals ordered quantity minus on-hand
3.5Open Planned Orders (cprrp1100m000) at Planning➔Order Planning➔Planned Orders, for the items' planning cluster and siteWrite downplanned purchase ordersevery row at Order Status Planned
3.6Select the planned production order and run Pegging - UpstreamWrite downpegging arithmetic checkeach level's children sum to its requirement
Run MRP: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
The run plans the pair but not a componentThe component has no planning data of its own. Step 1.4 — MRP skips it silently
A component has plan data and still produces nothingIt may be correctly absent — planning proposes supply only for what stock does not cover. Read its own Item Order Plan and on-hand
The pegging tree is emptyPegging relations were not generated, or the demand is beyond the Pegging Horizon in Planning Parameters (cprpd0100m000)

4Cross the boundary

Result
The proposals become a real purchase order and a real production order.
Screen
Planning➔Order Planning➔Confirm Order Planning (cprrp1200m000)

Why LN works this way. A planned order is a proposal that no other module can see. Confirming marks it approved, and transferring translates it: a planned production order becomes a production order in Job Shop Control and a planned purchase order becomes a purchase order in Procurement, decided by the item's supply source. A transfer run against unconfirmed orders appears to do nothing.

Warning
Only the purchase half of this task has been walked. Step 4.8, the production half, is the one step nobody has performed — you are testing it, not using it.
StepActionYou should see
4.1Confirm BAM-ROD has a row on the Item - Business Partner tab of its purchase dataA buy-from business partner
4.2If MRP proposed a planned purchase order for BAM-SLEEVE, check the same tab for that itemA partner row, or the transfer will refuse it at step 4.7
4.3In Confirm Order Planning (cprrp1200m000), confirm the planned orders you intend to transferOrder Status moves from Planned to Confirmed
4.4Open Transfer Order Planning (cppat1210m000)
4.5Select PurchaseThe transfer is scoped to the purchase orders
4.6Select Error Report and Process Report
4.7Run the transfer and read the reportWrite downreal purchase order numberthe report names the order each proposal became, or why it did not transfer
4.8Repeat steps 4.4–4.7 with Job Shop selected instead of PurchaseWrite downreal production order numberexpected in Production Orders (tisfc0501m000) at Created
Cross the boundary: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
The transfer runs and nothing happensThe orders were still Planned. Step 4.3. There is no message for "nothing matched"
Buy-from BP cannot be determined for item …No partner row on the item's Item - Business Partner tab. Steps 4.1–4.2. The failed proposal survives, so fix it and rerun
Purchase Order Type is blankLN gives an error. The walked run defaulted IPO

5Receive the components

Result
Rods and sleeves are on hand at the raw-material warehouse.
Screen
Warehousing➔Orders➔Orders (whinh2100m000)

Why LN works this way. The purchase order generated an inbound warehousing order; receiving against it and confirming the receipt books the components into the raw-material warehouse. The on-hand figure, not the receipt status, is the proof.

StepActionYou should see
5.1Open Warehousing Orders (whinh2100m000)
5.2Find the inbound order LN raised from the purchase order. It is the order from step 4.7
5.3Click Drill InOrder type PUI "Purchase Receipts", ship-to the raw-materials warehouse
5.4Select the inbound lines and run Actions➔ReceiveWarehouse Receipt (whinh3512m000) opens
5.5Enter the packing-slip reference for each lineThe lines carry their references
5.6Confirm the receiptWrite downwarehouse receipt number; Status = Confirmed, All Lines Final and All Lines Complete both set
5.7Read Errors Logged
5.8Re-read BAM-ROD on-hand at the raw-materials warehouse in Inventory 360. The warehouse is from step 1.3Write downrod on-hand after receiptup by exactly the quantity received
Receive the components: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
No inbound order appears after the transferCheck the purchase order's Release to Warehousing tab; Purchase Order Line Status (tdpur4534m000) names the activity a stuck line is waiting on
whinh0032 at the receiptCapture the LOG detail before clearing it, and read Errors Logged and Receipt Message Log (whinh3530m000) afterwards
The receipt confirms but on-hand does not moveWhether All Lines Final and All Lines Complete were both set, and whether you re-read the warehouse from step 1.3

6Build the pairs

Result
The finished item is posted to inventory.
Screen
Manufacturing➔Job Shop➔Production Orders (tisfc0501m000)

Why LN works this way. The production order releases, issues the components from the warehouse to the work center, and on the last operation reported complete posts the finished pairs to inventory, silently or after asking depending on a parameter. Production Completed is the handoff to Warehousing, not a failed Completed.

StepActionYou should see
6.1Open the production order from step 4.8
6.2Check its BOM, routing and estimated materialsBOM rev 000002, routing 0 rev 000001, operation 10, rods and sleeves listed
6.3Select the order and run Actions➔Release OrdersRelease Production Orders (tisfc0204m000) opens
6.4Run the release for this order onlyOrder Status = Released; warehousing issue and receipt orders now exist
6.5Open Material to Issue for Production Orders (ticst0101m100) at Manufacturing➔Job Shop➔Production Materials➔Material to Issue for Production Orders
6.6Issue the materials. Follow steps 2–9Actual Quantity = the estimated quantity; Order Status = Active
6.7Open Report Operations (tisfc0130m000) at Manufacturing➔Job Shop➔Production Control➔Report Operations, enter the built quantity in Completed, and saveLN may ask whether to confirm the receipt automatically — record which way you answer
6.8Return to Production Orders and read Order StatusWrite downproduction order status after reportingProduction Completed or Completed
6.9Read BAM-CHOP-PAIR on-hand at the finished-goods warehouse in Inventory 360. The warehouse is from step 1.2Write downpair on-hand after buildup by the built quantity over step 1.2
Build the pairs: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
The order will not releasePrinting Production Order Documents Mandatory in tisfc0100s000 may require Printed first
The material line stays blockedRun Initiate Inventory Issue (tisfc0207m000) manually; if still blocked, record what you saw
Status reaches Production Completed and on-hand does not moveThat is the No path at step 6.7. Check Warehousing Orders (whinh2100m000) for an open production receipt order

7Ship

Result
Shipment Confirmed, on-hand down by the shipped quantity.
Screen
Warehousing➔Manager Dashboard (whinh2300m000)

Why LN works this way. The sales order from Create the demand is released to warehousing, advised, picked, frozen and confirmed, exactly as in Ship from stock. On-hand at the shipping warehouse down by the shipped quantity is the completion test for the whole chain.

StepActionYou should see
7.1In the sales order, Actions➔Release➔Release to Warehousing… per steps 2–5Log Report prints; a warehousing order exists under your sales order number
7.2In Warehouse Manager Dashboard (whinh2300m000), filter on your sales order number and Drill InWarehousing Order (whinh2100m100), Origin Sales, Type 20- SO/SC Out
7.3On the Outbound Lines tab, tick the line and run Actions➔Advice➔Generate AdviceAdvised and Released both fill; Picking List by Location prints
7.4In Picking List (whinh4525m100), tick the line
7.5Run Actions➔Pick RunLine status Staged
7.6Read Shipment on the order's Shipment Lines tabWrite downshipment number
7.7In Shipments (whinh4130m000), find the shipment and Drill In, then Actions➔FreezeStatus = Frozen; Confirm becomes available
7.8Actions➔ConfirmWrite downshipped quantity; Status = Confirmed, inventory relieved
7.9Re-read BAM-CHOP-PAIR on-hand at the warehouse from step 1.2Write downpair on-hand after shippingdown by exactly the shipped quantity
Ship: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
Advice greyed outYou are on the session toolbar. The advice actions live on the Outbound Lines toolbar — step 7.3
The order will not adviseThe header Warehouse does not hold the stock. Recheck against step 1.2
The shipment will not confirmThe line was never picked, or the shipment was never frozen. Steps 7.6 and 7.7

Variations

Variations
CaseWhat changes
Stock already covers the orderThe YES branch of the flowchart. Planning generates no planned orders, so nothing from Cross the boundary to Build the pairs happens — go straight to Ship from stock. MRP still runs; whether it generates anything depends on demand against on-hand plus on-order
The finished item is in the wrong warehouse to ship fromInsert Warehouse transfer between Build the pairs and Ship. On current evidence BAM-CHOP-PAIR is received and shipped at the same finished-goods warehouse, so this does not arise
Build by hand instead of from planning
Task 2		Skip step 4.8 and create the production order directly per Create the production order. This is the only production path that has been walked — it is the fallback if step 4.8 fails
Components already in stock
Task 4		this task transfers only the production side and Receive the components does not happen. This is the likely shape of a sleeve-only shortfall
Build by hand instead of from planning
Task 4		Skip step 4.8 and create the production order directly per Create the production order. This is the only production path that has been walked — it is the fallback if step 4.8 fails
Components already in stock
Task 5		Cross the boundary transfers only the production side and this task does not happen. This is the likely shape of a sleeve-only shortfall

What comes next

WhenThenStart at
The shipment is Confirmed and on-hand has decreasedThe procedure ends here. Invoicing the order is done in Financials, which this guide does not cover—
Actual costs need calculating and posting—

    The BOM is at revision 000002; revision 000001 is expired. Routing 0 revision 000001, operation 10, work center A1000. One site, with raw materials and finished goods in two warehouses.

    Warning. BAM-ROD has a buy-from business partner and BAM-SLEEVE has not been checked. A buy-from business partner was added to BAM-ROD because the transfer refused it without one. If MRP proposes a planned purchase order for BAM-SLEEVE, Cross the boundary will very likely fail on it the same way. Not documented for this release.
